title: Reading a firewall rule set from top to bottom
excerpt: Rules are read in order, which means the order is the policy. What I look for when I read one end to end.
body:
Firewall rules are evaluated in order, so the order *is* the policy. Reading a rule set from top to bottom, slowly, is one of the most useful afternoons I know.

What I look for:

- **Shadowed rules:** a broad rule above a narrow one means the narrow one never fires.
- **"Temporary" exceptions:** if a rule has a ticket number and no expiry, it's permanent now.
- **Any-to-any:** every `any` deserves a sentence explaining why.
- **Missing comments:** a rule nobody can explain is a rule nobody dares remove.

Rule sets grow by addition and almost never by subtraction. Reading them end to end is how they shrink.
